required_input_state: A numeric key variable and required closed interval bounds expressed as constants, variables, or system missing values; input variables for calculations must be numeric.
Observations with missing key values are excluded both as targets and as contributors, and by() variables are needed when ranges must remain within groups.
output_interface: new variables in the dataset in memory containing each requested interval statistic and r(newvars) listing their names
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: rangestat uses numeric key ranges and ignores tsset or xtset declarations; it is not a calendar-aware time-series window command.

if and in restrict both the observations receiving results and the observations contributing to intervals, while excludeself suppresses current input values without removing the observation from raw counts.

commands.role: Compute data-driven bandwidths for local-polynomial regression-discontinuity estimation and inference.
capabilities: Select MSE- or coverage-error-rate-optimal point-estimation and bias-correction bandwidths, either common or side specific.
Support sharp, fuzzy, kink, and fuzzy-kink designs with covariates, weights, kernels, mass-point adjustment, and documented variance estimators.
required_input_state: An outcome variable and a running variable; the cutoff defaults to zero.
Stata 16 or later; fuzzy treatment, covariates, weights, or cluster identifiers are conditional inputs.
output_interface: E-class bandwidth results, including e(mat_h), e(mat_b), method-specific scalar selectors, and design metadata.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Selects bandwidths but does not estimate an RD treatment effect or construct an RD plot.
MSE and coverage-error-rate selectors target different criteria, and common and side-specific selectors are distinct.

commands.role: Construct regression-discontinuity plots from binned outcome means and side-specific global polynomial fits.
capabilities: Use evenly or quantile-spaced bins with IMSE-optimal, variability-mimicking, or manually specified bin counts.
Add confidence intervals or shading, covariate adjustment, weights, mass-point handling, graph customization, and optional generated plot-data variables.
required_input_state: An outcome variable and a running variable; the cutoff defaults to zero.
Stata 16 or later; covariates and weights are conditional inputs.
output_interface: A Stata graph unless hide is specified, plus e-class bin counts, polynomial equations, and polynomial coefficients.
genvars optionally creates rdplot_* variables containing bin, mean, interval, and fitted-value data in memory.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Visualizes the discontinuity but does not provide the treatment-effect inference of rdrobust or the selector output of rdbwselect.
Manual nbins() precludes binselect(); p() and h() govern the plotted global polynomial fits rather than rdrobust's local-polynomial inference interface.

commands.role: Estimate local-polynomial regression-discontinuity effects with conventional and robust bias-corrected inference.
capabilities: Estimate sharp, fuzzy, kink, and fuzzy-kink designs using automatic or user-supplied point and bias bandwidths.
Support covariate adjustment, weights, kernels, mass-point handling, MSE or coverage-error-rate bandwidth selection, and documented heteroskedasticity- or cluster-robust variance estimators.
required_input_state: An outcome variable and a running variable; the cutoff defaults to zero.
Stata 16 or later; fuzzy treatment, covariates, weights, or cluster identifiers are conditional inputs.
output_interface: E-class effects, standard errors, p-values, confidence intervals, effective sample counts, bandwidths, and side-specific polynomial objects.
e(b) distinguishes Conventional, Bias-corrected, and Robust columns, with documented variances in e(V).
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Estimates the RD effect, unlike selector-only rdbwselect and visualization-only rdplot.
The bias-corrected coefficient paired with the conventional standard error is not the intended robust bias-corrected inferential object; the Robust pairing carries that inference.

commands.role: Transform values of numeric variables using ordered value, range, missing-value, or catch-all rules.
capabilities: Recode exact values, inclusive ranges, variable-specific min and max, system or extended missing values, and multiple variables.
Create generated or prefixed variables, define and attach value labels, copy unselected observations, and report overlapping or unused rules with test.
required_input_state: Numeric, non-alias variables in memory; with if or in, min and max are computed over the restricted observations.
output_interface: By default mutates the source variables in memory; generate() or prefix() instead creates new variables, optionally with value labels.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Rules are evaluated left to right and only the first match applies; keyword rules must come last, and else cannot be combined with missing or nonmissing.
Generated variables are missing outside an if or in selection unless copyrest is specified, whereas in-place recoding leaves those values unchanged; string and alias variables are unsupported.

commands.role: Fit ordinary or weighted least-squares linear regression.
capabilities: Accept factor-variable and time-series syntax together with analytic, frequency, importance, or probability weights.
Provide conventional, heteroskedasticity-robust, one- or multiway cluster-robust, HC2 or HC3, bootstrap, jackknife, and supported HAC or survey inference.
required_input_state: A dependent variable and any regressors in memory; cluster variables, weights, or survey settings are conditional inputs.
HAC variance estimation requires tsset data.
output_interface: Standard estimation state including e(b), e(V), e(sample), fit statistics, model tests, VCE metadata, and prediction or margins hooks.
Replay makes coefficient-table statistics available in r(table), which later r-class commands can replace.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Has no absorb() interface; robust or clustered VCE changes uncertainty calculations rather than adding fixed effects.
HAC disallows frequency, probability, and importance weights; probability weights disallow HC3; beta is incompatible with clustered VCE and svy.

commands.role: Fit linear least-squares regressions while absorbing one or more high-dimensional fixed effects.
capabilities: Absorb categorical interactions, heterogeneous slopes, and individual fixed effects in models with group-level outcomes.
Support robust, multiway-clustered, and Driscoll-Kraay VCEs and optionally save residuals or fixed-effect estimates.
required_input_state: absorb() identifiers and the ftools dependency are required for fixed-effect estimation; Driscoll-Kraay VCE requires tsset or xtset data.

Individual-FE models with group-level outcomes require long data uniquely identified by group and individual, group-constant outcomes and regressors, group() and individual(), and the individual identifier in absorb().
output_interface: Estimation results in e(b), e(V), and normally e(sample), plus absorbed-effect, cluster, degrees-of-freedom, singleton, iteration, and convergence metadata.
Optional residual and fixed-effect variables; documented tested postestimation is limited to estat summarize, predict, and test.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Singletons are dropped iteratively by default, degrees-of-freedom losses beyond two fixed effects are conservatively approximated, and saved fixed effects may not be identified.
Solver and tolerance choices trade speed against numerical accuracy, and fastregress is less numerically stable.
IV estimation and nonlinear Poisson fixed-effects models are outside this command; suest is documented as producing incorrect results after reghdfe.

commands.role: Change values of an existing variable for selected observations.
capabilities: Evaluate an expression under if, in, or by and report the number of actual changes.
Automatically promote numeric or string storage when replacement values require more capacity.
required_input_state: The target variable must already exist, cannot be an alias variable, and must be type-compatible with the expression.
output_interface: Mutates the target variable in the dataset in memory, potentially promoting its storage type.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Modifies existing data rather than creating a new variable and therefore cannot be abbreviated.
nopromote prevents storage expansion but can truncate replacement values to the existing type.

commands.role: Convert the active dataset between wide and long organization.
capabilities: Reshape multiple stubs with numeric or string j values, explicit j values, and @ placement within variable names.
Diagnose failed reshapes and retain definitions that permit argument-free reversal.
required_input_state: The data cannot contain alias variables; i() identifies logical observations and is required.
i() must be unique in wide data, i() plus j() must be unique in long data, and variables omitted from a long-to-wide reshape must be constant within i().
output_interface: Replaces the dataset layout in memory, creates j when going long, and drops j when going wide.
Stores dta[ReS...] dataset characteristics so reshape definitions can survive save and support later reversal.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: favor(speed) is faster but may require roughly twice the dataset's memory, whereas favor(memory) is slower.
Wide-to-long can represent absent stub variables with missing values and retain unintentionally omitted wide variables; broad or string stubs can capture similarly named variables unexpectedly.

commands.role: Compute randomization-inference or permutation-test p-values by resampling an assignment variable and rerunning a supplied command.
capabilities: Resample within strata or at an assignment-cluster level, hold treatment levels fixed, or use file-supplied or program-generated assignments.
Test nonzero sharp nulls with one- or two-sided statistics and optionally save draws, assignments, or a density graph.
required_input_state: A resampling variable, expressions retrievable after each execution, and a valid wrapped Stata command without a by prefix.
File-based assignments require resampvar1, resampvar2, and subsequent variables with valid match identifiers; program-based assignments require a compatible user program.
output_interface: Displayed observed and resampled statistics and p-values.
Optional .dta files containing collected estimates or resampled assignments, plus an optional density graph; the guide does not document a returned-result contract.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Monte Carlo precision depends on the replication count and RNG state; failed commands or missing statistics invalidate replications.
Default weak inequalities are conservative under ties, while strict is weakly overconfident and requires eps(0); weights require force.
cluster() constrains assignment resampling and does not request cluster-robust covariance estimation in the wrapped command.

commands.role: Persist the dataset currently in memory as a Stata .dta file.
capabilities: Use an explicit filename or the dataset's last-known c(filename), with .dta added when omitted.
Optionally include unattached value labels, e(sample), or an otherwise empty dataset.
required_input_state: A dataset in memory; omitting the filename requires a usable last-known filename.
An existing destination requires the replace option, and a zero-observation, zero-variable dataset requires emptyok.
output_interface: Writes a Stata-format dataset for later use and records the in-memory dataset as saved under that filename.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Provides Stata-native persistence rather than interchange-format export; older formats require saveold.
nolabel omits value-label definitions while retaining label-name associations, and alias variables must be dropped or materialized for older-version compatibility.

commands.role: Estimate the average treatment effect on the treated using synthetic difference-in-differences in group-by-time panels.
capabilities: Handle single-date or staggered adoption with optimally weighted units and periods under synthetic DID, DID, or synthetic-control methods.
Provide bootstrap, jackknife, placebo, or no inference; optimized or projected covariate adjustment; cluster-level resampling; and unit-weight, time-weight, or outcome-trend graphs.
required_input_state: Outcome, group, time, and treatment variables with treated and untreated units.
Bootstrap requires multiple treated units, jackknife requires multiple treated units within each adoption period, and placebo inference requires more controls than treated units.
output_interface: E-class ATT, confidence limits, standard error, e(b), e(V), adoption-specific effects, unit and time weights, adoption periods, and trend-series matrices.
returnweights adds weight variables to the dataset, and graph_export() writes graph files.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Bootstrap can be computationally expensive; jackknife is lighter but has stricter treated-unit requirements.
method(did) and method(sc) change the estimator rather than only its reporting, and sdid_event is a separate event-study wrapper.
Optimized and projected covariate adjustment use different procedures and comparison information; _not_yet changes the projected-adjustment comparison pool.

commands.role: Fit a stacked staggered-adoption event study that compares each treatment cohort with never-treated units.
capabilities: Create and append cohort-specific stacks, then estimate with unit-by-stack and time-by-stack fixed effects and unit-by-stack clustering through reghdfe.
Accept covariates, additional fixed effects, and optional stack interactions for covariates.
required_input_state: Long unit-time data with preconstructed lead and lag indicators, a treatment-cohort variable missing for never-treated units, numeric time, a never-treated indicator, and unit fixed-effect and clustering identifiers.
Requires avar, ftools, and reghdfe.
output_interface: Estimation results in e(b), e(V), and e(dof_table); the guide does not document a file export or stable stacked-dataset handoff.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Uses never-treated controls rather than already-treated or not-yet-treated comparisons.
Is a specialized stacked event-study estimator rather than a general two-way fixed-effects command and relies on external estimation dependencies.

commands.role: Fit Cox proportional-hazards models to survival-time data declared with stset.
capabilities: Handle single- or multiple-record data with single or multiple failures, stratified baseline hazards, shared gamma frailty, offsets, and time-varying covariate effects.
Provide Breslow, Efron, exact marginal, or exact partial tie handling and supported model-based, robust, clustered, bootstrap, jackknife, or survey inference.
required_input_state: Data must already be stset; analysis time, failures, subject identity, entry and exit, and weights are inherited from that declaration.
output_interface: E-class coefficients, covariance, estimation sample, subject and failure counts, risk time, tie method, VCE, strata or frailty metadata, and postestimation hooks.
Replay creates r(table); supported predictions include cumulative baseline hazard, survivor functions, residuals, and frailty effects.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Breslow is the fastest default but can approximate poorly with many ties; Efron and exact methods cost more, and exact partial can be very slow.
exactm and exactp are incompatible with tvc(), robust VCE, and clustered VCE; weights are unsupported with Efron and exact partial methods.
shared() is unavailable with delayed entry or gaps, and most predictions are unavailable after tvc().

commands.role: Declare and validate the in-memory dataset as survival-time data for downstream st commands.
capabilities: Define analysis time, observation windows, failures, subjects, origins, scaling, entry and exit, gaps, repeated failures, and weights for single- or multiple-record data.
Reset or display the declaration and support documented past- or future-history data management.
required_input_state: An exit-time variable; multiple-record declarations require id() and failure().
Weighted multiple-record data require weights that are constant within subject.
output_interface: Adds or recomputes _st, _d, _t, and _t0 and stores the survival declaration with the dataset for downstream st commands.
Marks excluded records rather than dropping them; stset, clear removes the declaration without removing substantive observations.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: origin(), enter(), and time0() represent different time concepts and are not substitutes.
Default exit(failure) excludes records after the first failure, so repeated-failure analysis requires an explicit alternative exit rule.
Many inconsistencies produce warnings and _st=0 exclusions rather than stopping execution, so the retained analysis sample must be inspected; stset is not an estimator.

commands.role: Calculate and display univariate descriptive statistics for numeric variables.
capabilities: Report observation count, mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum, with detail adding percentiles, skewness, kurtosis, variance, and extreme values.
Support grouped execution, factor variables, time-series operators, analytic, frequency, or importance weights, and a fast non-displaying meanonly interface.
required_input_state: Numeric variables in memory; omitting the varlist summarizes all applicable variables.
Importance weights cannot be combined with detail.
output_interface: Displayed summaries plus r-class scalars for the most recent variable, including N, mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, weighted sum, sum, and variance, with additional distribution statistics under detail.
Does not mutate the dataset or create a persistent table object.
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: meanonly cannot be combined with detail and suppresses variance calculation.
Provides descriptive statistics rather than confidence intervals for means; factor-variable summaries are indicator means or proportions rather than cumulative category tables.

commands.role: Create one- or multiway tables of frequencies, summary statistics, ratios, and results collected from Stata commands.
capabilities: arrange repeated statistic() and command() results across row, column, and separate-table dimensions
collect posted r() or e() results into the default or a named collection for later collect customization
format and export the table directly to DOCX, HTML, PDF, Excel, LaTeX, SMCL, text, or Markdown
required_input_state: A dataset and the required grouping or statistic variables must be in memory; strL variables are not allowed.
Results named in command() must be posted by the embedded command, while if, in, and weights are specified on table itself.
Frequency, analytic, importance, and probability weights are supported.
output_interface: displayed table, the default Table or a named collection, r(N), and optional markvar() indicator or exported table file
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Unlike tabstat, table supports n-way layouts and command-result collection; unlike tabulate, it does not expose the same dedicated one- or two-way association tests, indicator generation, or frequency matrices.
Without listwise, requested statistics can use variable-specific nonmissing samples; file append is limited to HTML, LaTeX, SMCL, text, or Markdown, while Excel uses modify, sheet(), and cell().

commands.role: Display selected summary statistics for multiple numeric variables in one compact table, optionally by one grouping variable.
capabilities: report chosen location, dispersion, count, percentile, and shape statistics
calculate statistics for each level of one numeric or string by() variable and switch whether variables or statistics form the columns
save overall and group-specific statistics as r() matrices
required_input_state: Numeric variables must be in memory; only analytic and frequency weights are supported.
The default uses each variable's available observations, while casewise requests a common complete-case sample.
output_interface: displayed compact table and, with save, r(StatTotal), group matrices r(Stat#), and group-name macros r(name#)
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Its by() option accepts one grouping variable, and it has no native n-way row, column, and separate-table layout or direct file export.
It summarizes numeric variables without replacing the dataset; it does not provide tabulate's contingency-table association tests or collapse's aggregate dataset.

commands.role: Produce a one-way frequency distribution or a two-way contingency table with optional percentages and association tests.
capabilities: report one-way frequencies, percentages, cumulative percentages, and an optional relative-frequency plot
report two-way cell, row, and column percentages with documented chi-squared, exact, and ordinal association measures
store frequency and level matrices, generate one-way category indicators, or place results in a Tabulate collection
required_input_state: One or two categorical variables must be in memory.

Frequency, analytic, and importance weights are accepted, but analytic and importance weights are incompatible with Pearson or likelihood-ratio chi-squared and several association measures; exact tests can be memory intensive for large tables.
output_interface: displayed table; r() counts and requested test statistics; optional matrices, indicator variables, graph, or Tabulate collection
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Its direct table is limited to one or two dimensions, unlike table's n-way layouts and mixed command results.

Its core output is categorical frequencies and association measures rather than tabstat-style numeric summaries; generate() adds variables, and file output from a Tabulate collection requires a separate collect export step.

commands.role: Perform postestimation Wald tests over coefficient sets selected with Stata varlist notation.
capabilities: jointly test selected coefficients against zero or, with equal, against one another
expand factor-variable, time-series, range, and wildcard notation and restrict matching to a specified equation by name or number
apply documented survey adjustment or a specified denominator degree of freedom
required_input_state: Active estimation results with a coefficient vector and covariance matrix are required, and the current dataset is used to expand the varlist.
output_interface: displayed F or chi-squared test and r(p), r(F) or r(chi2), degrees of freedom, and dropped-constraint indicators
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It selects coefficient sets by varlist and does not express arbitrary linear combinations, constants, cross-equation equalities, or nonlinear restrictions.
Expanded variables absent from the fitted model are ignored, and testparm has no accumulate or multiple-testing-adjustment interface.

commands.role: Perform postestimation Wald tests of simple or composite linear restrictions on fitted-model parameters.
capabilities: test coefficients or linear combinations against constants and impose within- or cross-equation equalities
accumulate restrictions and report individual plus joint tests with documented multiple-testing adjustments
save the variance-covariance matrix of the tested linear combinations with matvlc()
required_input_state: Active fitted-model coefficients and their estimated covariance matrix are required.
output_interface: displayed F or chi-squared test; r(p), r(F) or r(chi2), degrees of freedom, and dropped constraints; optional r(mtest) and r(mtmethod)
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It handles linear restrictions only; nonlinear restrictions require a different interface and likelihood-ratio tests are distinct from its covariance-based Wald test.
Asterisk and hyphen are arithmetic operators rather than varlist wildcards or ranges, and redundant or inconsistent constraints may be dropped.

commands.role: Convert numeric variables to string variables by generating new variables or replacing the originals.
capabilities: generate one string variable for each numeric source or replace the source variables in place
control string representations with an explicit numeric format or each variable's display format
preserve or copy variable labels and characteristics and record conversion characteristics
required_input_state: Numeric source variables must be in memory, and exactly one of generate() or replace is required.
generate() must name one new variable per source; a conversion that is not reversible is refused unless force is specified.
output_interface: new string variables or in-place string replacements in the active dataset, with conversion characteristics attached to each converted variable
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It stringifies underlying numeric values rather than decoding value-label text, and force can allow information-losing conversion.
format() and usedisplayformat are mutually exclusive; generate() preserves the numeric sources whereas replace removes them.

commands.role: Add observations for missing time points in an already declared time series or panel time series.
capabilities: fill gaps within a single series or within each panel's observed endpoints
extend every panel to the dataset-wide minimum and maximum time with full, producing a strongly balanced time span
required_input_state: The dataset must be tsset or xtset with a time variable; full is available only for panel data.
output_interface: additional in-memory observations with the time identifier and, when specified, the panel identifier filled, and all other variables missing
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It changes the observation topology but does not interpolate or impute non-key variables.
Default panel filling preserves panel-specific endpoints, while full may add observations outside them; filling gaps is not required for time-series operators to respect the declared time variable.

commands.role: Declare and manage a single time series or a panel time series with a panel and time variable.
capabilities: set the time unit, display format, and delta used by time-series operators
display, clear, and persist the declaration with the saved dataset
activate lag, lead, difference, and seasonal-difference operators and ts commands, plus xt commands when panelvar and timevar are both declared
required_input_state: Time and optional panel variables must be numeric and integer valued, and the declared delta must fit the observed spacing.
output_interface: persistent dataset time-series metadata, data sorted in declared order, and r() macros and scalars describing variables, range, delta, gaps, units, and balance
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It declares time structure but neither fills gaps nor balances panels, and the delta determines how operators locate adjacent periods.
The panel-time form is equivalent to xtset panelvar timevar, but tsset has a timevar-only form and no panelvar-only form.

commands.role: Compose one or more plot types on numeric y and x scales into a single two-way graph.
capabilities: overlay heterogeneous plot types using parenthesized specifications or double-bar separators
apply sample restrictions and options to individual plots or to the overall composite graph
combine data-rendering, fitted or transformed, immediate, and function plot types
required_input_state: The chosen plot types require compatible numeric axes and their documented varlists, immediate arguments, or function specifications.
output_interface: one graph containing the requested plots, with saving() available as a graph twoway option
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Plot-specific options cannot be supplied at the overall twoway level, and plot-level versus command-level if or in restrictions have different scope.
Multiple y variables may share one x variable in a scatter specification, but different x variables require separate plot specifications.

commands.role: Test one-sample, independent two-sample, or paired-sample hypotheses about means.
capabilities: compare one sample mean with a specified value or compare two groups defined by by()
treat two variables as matched pairs or, with unpaired, as independent samples
for unpaired comparisons, use equal-variance, Satterthwaite unequal-variance, or Welch inference, and reverse the reported by() group contrast
required_input_state: Numeric outcome variables are required; by() must identify two groups, and paired variables must represent matched observations in the same rows.
No active estimation result is required.
output_interface: displayed means, uncertainty, confidence intervals, t statistic, degrees of freedom, and one- and two-sided p-values, with corresponding sample and test quantities in r()
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It tests raw mean hypotheses rather than restrictions on fitted-model coefficients and has no documented weight or arbitrary VCE interface.
Two variables are paired by default unless unpaired is specified, by() implies independent samples, and the command does not jointly compare more than two groups.

commands.role: Load a Stata-format dataset, or a selected variable and observation subset, into current memory.
capabilities: load a complete .dta dataset from a local path or URL
load only named variables and observations selected by if or in
omit saved value-label definitions with nolabel
required_input_state: An accessible dataset saved in Stata format is required; clear is needed to discard changed, unsaved data already in memory.
output_interface: the requested complete dataset or subset replaces the current in-memory dataset, with saved value labels loaded unless nolabel is specified
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It replaces the active data in memory and loads Stata-format datasets rather than non-Stata formats.
Older Stata versions may not read newer file formats, and Stata/BE can load SE or MP files only when their dimensions fit BE limits.

commands.role: Winsorize or trim numeric variables at specified percentile cutpoints.
capabilities: cap tail values at the cutpoints or, with trim, set tail values to missing
apply default, custom, or one-sided cutpoints and calculate them separately within by() groups
generate suffixed variables or overwrite the original variables
required_input_state: Numeric target variables and any by() grouping variables must be in memory.
output_interface: new variables with _w, _tr, or a requested suffix, or overwritten source variables when replace is specified
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Trimming changes outlying values to missing rather than dropping observations, whereas winsorizing caps them.
replace cannot be combined with suffix(), and by() uses group-specific rather than pooled cutpoints.

commands.role: Fit linear panel-data instrumental-variables models using random-effects, between-effects, fixed-effects, or first-differenced 2SLS estimators.
capabilities: estimate G2SLS or EC2SLS random effects and between-, fixed-, or first-differenced 2SLS models
separate endogenous regressors from excluded instruments in the model syntax and optionally display first-stage regressions
use conventional, robust, one-way clustered, bootstrap, or jackknife covariance estimates
required_input_state: The panel variable must be xtset; first-differenced estimation also requires a declared time variable.
The excluded-instrument count must be at least the endogenous-regressor count; the command documents no weights, and first-differenced models do not allow factor variables.
output_interface: e-class estimates including e(b), e(V), e(sample), endogenous and exogenous variable lists, model and VCE metadata, panel counts, fit measures, variance components, and predict or margins handoff metadata
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: Unlike xtreg it supports explicit panel IV estimation but not correlated random effects, random-effects ML, population-averaged models, or additional-effect absorption.

Fixed effects do not identify time-invariant covariate coefficients; the regress option retains varlist2 as regressors, treats all covariates as exogenous, and ignores only the excluded-instrument list varlistiv.

commands.role: Fit linear panel-data models using random-effects, correlated-random-effects, between-effects, fixed-effects, random-effects maximum-likelihood, or population-averaged estimators.
capabilities: estimate GLS random effects, Mundlak correlated random effects, between effects, within fixed effects, Gaussian random-effects ML, or Gaussian identity-link GEE
absorb additional categorical effects in fixed-effects models and use model-specific robust, clustered, resampling, HC2, HC3, or Driscoll-Kraay covariance estimators where documented
return model-specific variance components and fit measures, Mundlak or panel-effect tests where applicable, and an estimated working-correlation matrix for population-averaged estimation
required_input_state: A panel variable must be xtset; population-averaged correlation structures other than exchangeable and independent, and fixed-effects Driscoll-Kraay VCE, also require a declared time variable.
Permitted weights and covariance estimators differ by model, and allowed weights must be constant within panel.
output_interface: model-specific e-class estimates including e(b), e(V), e(sample), panel counts, fit and variance-component results, VCE metadata, and predict or margins handoff state
population-averaged estimation stores e(cmd)=xtgee, e(cmd2)=xtreg, and e(R) for the estimated working-correlation matrix
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: It has no endogenous-regressor or excluded-instrument syntax; xtivreg supplies panel 2SLS, and xtreg does not fit dynamic-panel GMM.

Fixed effects do not estimate time-invariant regressor coefficients; model-specific weight and VCE options are not interchangeable; the continuous and categorical-by-continuous absorb() extension, HC3, Driscoll-Kraay, and apcriterion() are marked StataNow-only.

commands.role: Declare and manage panel data, optionally including a time variable and time-series settings within panels.
capabilities: declare panelvar alone or panelvar with timevar
set time units, display format, and delta when time is declared
display, clear, and persist the declaration, activate xt commands, and activate panel-aware time-series operators when timevar is specified
required_input_state: Panel and optional time variables must be numeric and integer valued; with time declared, the delta must fit observed spacing.
output_interface: persistent panel and optional time metadata plus r() macros and scalars describing variables, range, delta, gaps, units, and panel balance; time-declared data are sorted by panel and time
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: A panel-only declaration does not establish within-panel time order or enable time-series operators and is not resorted by an argument-free xtset.
It reports rather than fills gaps or balances panels; xtset panelvar timevar is equivalent to the two-variable tsset form, while only xtset supports panelvar alone.

commands.role: Fit linear dynamic panel models designed for small-T, large-N data by difference or system GMM with explicit internal and standard instrument construction.
capabilities: estimate default system GMM or difference GMM using first differences, or forward orthogonal deviations in the Mata implementation
build GMM-style and IV-style instrument sets with lag, equation, collapse, or principal-component controls
fit one- or two-step models with robust or cluster-defined covariance estimation, including multiway clustering, and report serial-correlation and overidentification diagnostics
required_input_state: Panel-time data must be tsset, and regressors must be classified by their exogeneity and valid lag moments.
System GMM requires the additional orthogonality conditions that justify instruments for the level equation.
output_interface: e-class estimates including coefficients, covariance, sample, panel and time metadata, instrument count and specification, Sargan and where applicable Hansen and difference-in-Sargan or Hansen tests, and Arellano-Bond tests; predict fitted values or residuals in levels or first differences, with optional saved matrices or variables in Mata speed mode
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: System GMM adds a level equation and instruments beyond difference GMM but relies on additional initial-condition assumptions.

Instrument proliferation can overfit instrumented variables and weaken Hansen tests; collapse reduces instrument width and computation but lowers large-sample efficiency, while lag limits or PCA reduce the GMM-style instrument count by restricting or replacing the set.
Two-step uncorrected standard errors can be downward biased, while twostep robust invokes the documented Windmeijer correction.

Holding the instrument set fixed, first differences and orthogonal deviations give identical coefficients in balanced panels, while orthogonal deviations can preserve more observations when panels contain gaps.

commands.role: Prefix supported Stata commands to write their results and user-assembled text or statistics to a Word or RTF document.
capabilities: export summary, correlation, frequency and tabulation results, means, proportions, ratios, t-tests, and regression results in detailed, nested, or wide table layouts
write lists, matrices, variable descriptions, text, and custom rows assembled from returned statistics
append to, replace, or continue compatible table structures within the output document
required_input_state: The wrapped command and its required data state must be available, and the destination must be writable.
Unrecognized user-written regression output requires a compatible standard r(table) and can be identified with isreg; wmat and survey-prefixed uses require an existing matrix or survey declaration.
output_interface: Myfile.doc in the current directory by default, or a save()-named .doc or .rtf file; replace overwrites, append continues the file, and when both are omitted asdoc appends if the target exists and otherwise creates it, with rowappend and table-continuation modes for compatible structures
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: This guide version documents Word or RTF rather than native DOCX, XLSX, or TeX output, and asdoc is an exporter rather than an estimator.
Nonstandard result-window output may be less structured, commands with no displayed output may add nothing, and some wrapped commands or options have documented parsing and layout limits.

commands.role: Replace the in-memory dataset with overall or grouped summary-statistic observations using the ftools aggregation interface.
capabilities: compute means, medians, percentiles, sums, nonmissing counts and percentages, extrema, interquartile ranges, and first or last variants in one clist
aggregate by numeric or string groups or produce one overall observation
merge collapsed statistics back to the original observations, append collapsed rows, create raw frequencies, or register custom Mata aggregators
required_input_state: A dataset and source variables must be in memory; string sources are limited to first, last, firstnm, and lastnm.
Weight support is partial and zero weights are ignored; register() requires matching aggregate_* Mata functions.
output_interface: a summary-statistics dataset in memory by default, the original observations augmented under merge, or original plus collapsed rows under append; optional frequency variable and no documented returned-results interface
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: The default operation replaces observation-level data with aggregate rows.
smart may invoke collapse when the data are already sorted because collapse might then be faster.
fast does not restore the original dataset after Break and may leave the data unusable.

The merge option adds collapsed statistics back to the original data and is documented as faster than egen or collapse followed by merge when the data are not sorted by the by() groups; append adds collapsed rows for totals.
Lower pool() values reduce memory use at a speed cost.

commands.role: Merge a using dataset into the in-memory master through the ftools join wrapper for one-to-one or many-to-one keys.
capabilities: perform 1:1 or m:1 key merges and limit variables read from the using data
retain or require selected match outcomes with keep() and assert(), and create, name, or suppress the merge marker
copy value-label definitions and notes and optionally display the underlying join command
required_input_state: A master dataset must be in memory, a using dataset and valid 1:1 or m:1 keys must be supplied, and the operation must not require update or replace semantics.
output_interface: merged observations and variables in memory, _merge or a generate()-named marker unless suppressed, copied labels and notes unless disabled, and no documented returned-results interface
tradeoffs_and_incompatibilities: The maintainer guide documents only 1:1 and m:1 joins.
update and replace are explicitly unavailable.
force and sorted are accepted but ignored.
verbose is an added diagnostic option that displays debug information and the underlying join command.
